chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Auditioning for Fletcher Henderson without saying who he was
summary: After his mother's death he moved to New York in 1940 and won the Henderson guitar job without revealing that Henderson knew his mother, telling him six months later on a bus in Mississippi.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x:
Yeah, he said, but I'm over age. But any way, I never was -- I never tried to play like Charlie, still don't. But now, I told you that I was with Fletcher Henderson. I went to New York -- after my mother died I went to New York to live, 1938, '39, some time ago, '40. 1940. I had been to New York previously with Roy Eldridge. And this is really when I met Dizzy, was in 1937, at the Savoy Ballroom, when I was there with Roy Eldridge. But I went back in 1940 to live, and someone told me, I think Sid Catlett or someone told me that Fletcher was having auditions for guitar player.

Now, I knew that if I told him who I was I would have had the job automatically, you know, because my mother was very good friends. She had introduced me to him at the Savoy Ballroom in Chicago quite a few years before but he wouldn't have remembered me. So fine. So I went to audition for this job, and I never told him who I was, and I got the job, incidently, and I worked with him about six months before I told him who I was. We were riding on the bus one day in Mississippi or someplace, and I said, Fletcher, you really don't remember where I met you. He said, no, John. I said, well my mother, Georgia Garham. And he died, you know. Why

didn't you tell me? But I had to get the job this way. Now, we'll go back again. I told you that I went to New York for the first time with Roy Eldridge. I worked with Roy. When he left Fletcher he formed a band, this was in '36. And I worked with Roy, I was in his band in Chicago, the Three Deuces. We had a tremendous band. But before that I had worked at the Three Deuces at Tatum for about two years. Now, this was --
